activities.description: Astronaut travels past each planet as it's named in the song.
Astronaut returns to a zoomed-out view of the inner solar system.
Astronaut visits Earth, Mars, Venus, then Mercury, while a box displays the planet name and the number of moons.
Astronaut repeats the journey past each planet.
Astronaut explores the asteroid belt. A box appears next to Jupiter, displaying its name and the number of moons.

videoEditingDetails.description: Visual shift to focus on the inner planets.
Transition to a darker scene for the asteroid belt.

activities.description: Astronaut continues past Jupiter and the remaining planets.
Astronaut visits Saturn and Uranus while a box displays each planet and the number of moons.
Astronaut repeats the journey past each planet, ending with a focus on Pluto. Each planet's name and number of moons are displayed in a box.

youtube_description:
I wrote this song to teach my one-year-old daughter about the solar system (she is a big fan of space!).

Available on iTunes:
http://itunes.apple.com/gb/album/the-planet-song/id516158024?i=516158027

Amazon:
http://www.amazon.co.uk/The-Planet-Song/dp/B007R1ZRKI

CD Baby:
http://www.cdbaby.com/cd/matthogg2


Recorded at Mike's Place Studio.

Acoustic Guitar, Bass and Drums all expertly performed by Mike Sunderland.


LYRICS:

There's Mercury, Venus, Earth,
Mars and Jupiter,
Saturn, Uranus and Neptune,
Last of all there's Pluto too.

The first four planets are rocky,
They orbit near the Sun.
Earth has one moon, Mars has two,
Venus and Mercury have none!

Next there is the Asteroid Belt,
Made of ice and rocks.
Then there's giant Jupiter,
With its great big red spot.

Saturn is the next planet,
Its rings are very wide.
Uranus also has rings
And spins 'round on its side.

Neptune's the last gas giant,
And Pluto's last of all.
It's now classed as a dwarf planet,
Because it's very small.


Music and Lyrics by Matt Hogg.
